answer: Agents coordinating a survey voyage record each mapped knoll in a shared thread, but task allocation is weighted by tokens locked in escrow, not by the number of accounts. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake agents gives the same total allocation weight as staking them through one agent. To capture a larger share of paid work, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens for the full escrow period, tying up capital that could earn returns elsewhere.
